findings.finding: F1 — the spec's tap seed cannot work: referenceRouteFromHref (web/src/features/refs/routes.ts:396-437) resolves a same-origin path such as /issues/CORE-1 exactly as it resolves dispatch://, and collectReferenceAnchors (web/src/features/refs/RefLink.tsx:134-157) then rewrites the anchor, calls replaceChildren() and adds a hover preview, so the author's text is gone.
findings.answer: Plan T5 and departure D1: the primary observable becomes the anchor that receives the tap's click, recorded by a capture-phase listener that prevents the default; a small navigating arm uses a same-origin path that is not an issue, project-document or agent-artifact route, and the plan requires asserting that the seeded anchor keeps its text and has a null data-dispatch-ref before it is used.

findings.finding: F2 — every probe the row makes sits inside the anchor's own text or border box (phone.e2e.ts:471-495, :501-535), so deleting .prose a { padding-block: 3px } cannot fail it; the mutation acceptance needs a new check whose probe is not self-referential.
findings.answer: Plan T4 commits in advance to a probe at a fixed offset below the upper link's own text bottom (upperText.bottom + 1 as the candidate), forbids deriving the probe from the padded getBoundingClientRect(), and requires the real numbers to be measured before the offset is fixed. Recorded as departure D2.

findings.finding: F3 — .prose pitch is inherited per call site (styles.css:424-426), so the 24px pitch the 3px budget rests on is not the tightest: the Inbox ask card is about 24.4px (AskCard.tsx:522-523) and a text-xs body sits on a 16px pitch (AgentThread.tsx:112-113).
findings.answer: Plan T6 requires the enumeration of every .prose call site below 1280px with its measured font-size and line-height, scopes the page change to the two surfaces the row measures, and puts the wider question to the architect as Q3 with that default.

findings.finding: F4 — the repeat count: the human called 200 attempts a waste, the 0.94s cost note excludes the per-repeat database reset and context setup, and a count alone does not prove 'the same answer every time'.
findings.answer: Overtaken by spec v18, which the architect published while this plan was drafted: the proof is --repeat-each=30 at the fix's head paired with the same command at the commit before the fix, where the row must fail at least once. Plan T3a and T7(2) carry exactly that pairing, and T3a raises the count if thirty pre-fix repeats all pass.

findings.finding: F5 — 'the page was still laying itself out' cannot by itself be the mechanism: the rect and the hit test are one synchronous page.evaluate, and 'not-a-link' means a real element was topmost and was inside neither seeded anchor.
findings.answer: The plan states that explicitly in 'What is already established', lists four live hypotheses instead of a cause, and T3b specifies the instrumentation that separates them: the whole document.elementsFromPoint stack with each entry's tag, test id, classes, computed z-index and position and rect, both anchors' rects, how many main a match each seeded name, scroll offsets, readyState and devicePixelRatio.

findings.finding: F6 — the four retained artifacts are the only picture of a failure and they expire; only one was extracted locally.
findings.answer: Plan T1 downloads all four attempts to /legion before anything else and records each artifact's expiry; the pod has no unzip, so the plan names python3 zipfile for extraction.

findings.finding: F7 — four separate runs each need the INFRA-43 harness, built from scratch in a pod with no root, no Docker, no Postgres and no Playwright browsers, and every stylesheet mutation needs a rebuilt bundle.
findings.answer: Plan T0 makes the harness the first task with its own acceptance (setup script and env file on /legion, per-role port and database lane, psql on PATH, browsers installed) and every later task names bun run build:web between a stylesheet edit and the run that reads it.

findings.finding: F8 — Chromium's tap-target adjustment can make every tap follow the link whether or not the padding is present, so the hundred taps may not bear on the padding at all.
findings.answer: Plan T5 requires two arms: the padded arm and a control arm with the three pixels removed and the bundle rebuilt, both counts on the pull request, and says that if both arms always follow the link the pull request reports that the measurement does not bear on the padding rather than concluding that no reader can miss it.

findings.finding: F9 — is the hundred-tap measurement a throwaway script or a permanent row every pull request pays for (workers: 1, fullyParallel: false)?
findings.answer: Plan question Q2 to the architect, with the default written into T5 and T7(1): the measurement does not merge as a hundred-tap row, its numbers are quoted on the pull request, and the permanent guard is T4's mutation-sensitive probe plus, if the page changes, the before/after row.

findings.finding: F10 — 'the whole browser job stays green' has no machine-checkable form against a suite that is intermittently red for other reasons (INFRA-76).
findings.answer: Plan T7(4) restates it as one named whole-suite run at the fix's head with its summary quoted, every failure outside packages/dispatch/e2e/phone.e2e.ts triaged to its issue, and none inside it.

specDepartures.spec: The tap measurement needs links that lead somewhere inside Dispatch: a plain relative address such as /issues/CORE-1, which the markdown engine leaves as an ordinary link whose text the measurement can still find; the observable is the link being followed, the way hover-preview.e2e.ts taps a link and waits for the page it opens.
specDepartures.plan: The primary observable for the hundred taps is the anchor that receives the tap's click, recorded by a capture-phase click listener that prevents the default, on the externally addressed links the row already seeds; a separate arm of about five taps on a same-origin path that is not a reference route confirms that such a click opens its page.
specDepartures.evidence: referenceRouteFromHref (packages/dispatch/web/src/features/refs/routes.ts:396-437) resolves any same-origin href with new URL(href, appOrigin) and matches it with parseIssuePath, so /issues/CORE-1 returns an issue route exactly as dispatch://CORE-1 does; collectReferenceAnchors (packages/dispatch/web/src/features/refs/RefLink.tsx:134-157) then rewrites the href, sets data-dispatch-ref and calls anchor.replaceChildren(), removing the author's text, and RefPreview.tsx:33-36 gives it the hover card the spec wanted to avoid.

acceptance: The seeded link of the tap measurement is not /issues/CORE-1 but a same-origin path that is not an issue, project-document or agent-artifact route, asserted to keep its author's text and a null data-dispatch-ref.
'The link is followed' is observed as the click delivered to the anchor, with navigation proven on a few taps rather than on all hundred.

specDepartures.spec: The row still measures the hit box after the fix; the row as it stands may well survive the mutation, and where that is what the run shows, this work gives it a check that fails with the rule gone and passes with it present.
specDepartures.plan: The plan commits in advance to the new check rather than waiting for the mutation run to show the old one survives: a probe at a fixed offset below the upper link's own text bottom, with the offset measured from the seeded turn and never derived from the padded bounding rectangle.
specDepartures.evidence: Both probes of the row sit inside the anchor's own text or border box: the Conversation measurement probes upperText.bottom - 1 where upperText is the range rect with padding excluded (packages/dispatch/e2e/phone.e2e.ts:471-495), and check 5 probes firstRect.y + firstRect.height - 1, the anchor's own border box (:501-535). Neither can change when padding-block: 3px is deleted.

specDepartures.spec: A page change also corrects what the repository says about these rules, the note above them in packages/dispatch/web/src/styles.css and every sentence about them in packages/dispatch/AGENTS.md.
specDepartures.plan: The documentation duty covers four places: styles.css:88-101, AGENTS.md:281 and :287, the row's own header comment at packages/dispatch/e2e/phone.e2e.ts:388-392, and the load-bearing comment at packages/dispatch/web/src/features/inbox/BlockedOnYou.tsx:122-124.
specDepartures.evidence: Both code comments state the below-1280px link rule and would go stale with a page change: phone.e2e.ts:388-392 states the padding-not-overlay rationale, and BlockedOnYou.tsx:122-124 states that an unlayered a:not(.prose a) { display: inline-flex } beats Tailwind's block there.

outcome.scope: The page-change branch's documentation task covers two further files beyond the two the spec names; nothing is dropped.

specDepartures.spec: The code that pull request changed is also not on the path this row exercises; and the row asks which element a tap one pixel above the bottom of the link's text would reach, which the row reads as a tap there opening it.
specDepartures.plan: Neither sentence is carried into the work. The plan rests the 'no change caused this' conclusion on the identical tree (da145f8158ce carrying 5d969376f854) passing and failing and on the row reproducing at one head, and it treats document.elementFromPoint as a hit test rather than a tap, with T5 as the only place a tap is measured.
specDepartures.evidence: The browser suite runs the real Go Dispatch server built from packages/envoy (packages/dispatch/AGENTS.md:815-825), the dispatch CI filter includes packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/** (.github/workflows/envoy-and-contracts.yaml:373-377), and pmdoc.LineFeeds is applied to an ask's question on the write path this row seeds (packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/api/asks.go:324-328). A browser's hit test is not its tap behaviour: Chromium performs tap-target adjustment, which packages/dispatch/e2e/touch.ts does not control.
